forecast-period.text: A trough of low pressure near the NT border. A slow moving high pressure system in the Tasman Sea maintains a ridge across eastern parts of the state. A trough of low pressure over the far west is forecast to slowly move eastwards on Friday. Another trough and multiple cold fronts move over the state over the weekend. A ridge of high pressure moves into the west on Monday.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Showers and possible thunderstorms in the north, extending broadly across the state during the afternoon. Maximum temperatures above average, grading to well above average in the east. North to northwesterly winds ahead of a south to southwesterly change in the west, extending eastwards to reach the southeast during the afternoon, fresh at times about western coasts.

Showers and possible thunderstorms across the pastoral districts. Possible showers about the West Coast district. East to northeasterly winds, tending north to northwesterly ahead of a southwest to southeasterly change in the west during the day. Local afternoon sea breezes.

Showers and possible thunderstorms in the south, extending broadly across the state during the afternoon, tending to rain at times. Maximum temperatures above to near average, grading to below average in the west. North to northwesterly winds ahead of a fresh and gusty south to southwesterly change extending throughout the day.

Showers and possible thunderstorms, contracting northeastwards during the day. Showers redeveloping about the agricultural area. Maximum temperatures below average grading to well below average in the northwest. Fresh and gusty southwesterly winds.

text.p: Showers about the agricultural area and western coasts. Showers and possible thunderstorms about the far north. Maximum temperatures below average. South to southwesterly winds.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Monday: 2 to 10 mm broadly across SA. Possible falls of 10 to 20 mm about parts of the agricultural areas, western coasts. Heavier falls of 20 to 50 mm are possible with thunderstorms.
